title: Refresh a stale topic in place instead of creating a second one
intent: REFRESH mode and the single hardest rail in the ingestion prompt: 'writing without item_id creates a second topic, which is a failure.' Also grades carry-forward — the updated source restates three unchanged facts and changes three, so a refresh that only transcribes the new page loses the license and serving-footprint facts a future reader needs.
prompt: Our Kimi K3 topic is out of date. Refresh it and tell me what changed.

source_facts: The seeded topic is topics/kimi-k3.md, learned 2026-07-16, source_url https://moonshot.ai/blog/kimi-k3.
That URL now serves a page updated 2026-07-22 covering the K3.1 checkpoint.
Changed: context 512K to 768K; a vision variant K3.1-VL with a 1.1B-parameter encoder now exists; SWE-bench Verified 74.2% to 76.8%; pricing $0.55/$2.20 to $0.40/$1.60 per million tokens.
Unchanged and still true: 1.2T total / 32B active / 8 of 384 experts, modified MIT license with attribution above 100M MAU, ~640GB full-precision serving footprint, FP8 fits one 8xH200 node.
K3.0 weights stay downloadable and supported through year end; the kimi-k3 API alias now points at K3.1.
The seeded topic's line 'Text only; there is no vision variant at launch' is now false and must not survive the refresh.
traps: Writing a second topic (no item_id) is the failure this task exists for. It looks successful in the agent's own report.
Replacing the body with only the K3.1 delta silently deletes the license and serving-footprint facts.
Leaving the stale 'no vision variant' sentence in place while also adding the vision paragraph produces a self-contradicting topic.
Reporting 'nothing changed' or refusing to state the diff — the prompt asks for it explicitly.
judge.guidance: Score change_reporting on whether the final answer names the specific diffs rather than saying the topic was updated. Score carry_forward on whether facts the new page restates as unchanged survive in the stored body.
